title: Smoky Salmon and Sweet Corn Chowder
intro: This hearty New England-inspired chowder relies on tender potatoes and a partial mash to build creaminess naturally. Salmon and sweet corn keep the bowl satisfying without the need for heavy cream.

ingredients.name: Baby red potatoes
ingredients.canonical_name: Potatoes, red, flesh and skin, raw

ingredients.name: Low-sodium vegetable broth
ingredients.canonical_name: Soup, vegetable broth, ready to serve

ingredients.name: No-salt-added canned pink salmon
ingredients.canonical_name: Fish, salmon, pink, canned, drained solids

ingredients.name: Low-fat (1%) milk
ingredients.canonical_name: Milk, lowfat, fluid, 1% milkfat, with added vitamin A and vitamin D

instructions: Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium heat until shimmering, then add the onion and celery and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the smoked paprika and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the potatoes, sweet corn, and vegetable broth, and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium-high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover the pot, and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, checking the potatoes with a fork to ensure they are tender.
Mash a portion of the potatoes and corn directly in the pot using a potato masher or the back of a large spoon to naturally thicken the chowder.
Stir in the flaked salmon and the milk, and warm the chowder over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, ensuring the liquid does not boil.
Remove the pot from the heat, divide the chowder between bowls, and top with the fresh chives.
variation: Swap the pink salmon for drained no-salt-added canned white tuna.
conservation: Keeps 2-3 days refrigerated; reheat gently on the stovetop.
